analysis:
The PR changes only test fixtures and the test driver in libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/PlacementChecks. None of it is production code, and it does not touch attestation, authorization, key handling, encryption or the WebSocket boundary (TB-002, TB-009, TB-011).

1. Golden/layouts/gemma-4-26b.json (line 1): the golden layout now lists generationModes [pipeline_v1, tensor_parallel_v1]. It also adds routedExperts (128 experts, 8 selected) and a tensorParallel block: 2 ranks, float32 partials, reduction sealed_all_gather_sum_v1 (named as sealed, but the fixture does not show how it is sealed), and shardRule kernel_aligned_heads_and_channels_v1. The fixture only records the expected planner output. Whether the runtime seals the all-gather partials on the inter-rank link, and how this interacts with A-001 plaintext exposure to peer providers, is not visible here. The next pass should check the Gemma tensor-parallel implementation in the non-test source. It should also check that the runtime cannot select tensor-parallel mode unless that sealing is enforced.

2. Golden/pairs/m3ultra-m5ultra/expected.json: the planSHA256 and handOffPlanSHA256 values for the three gemma-4-26b variants changed (lines 46-48, 67-69, 88-90). Mode, cut and ranks are unchanged. The hashes were regenerated, probably because the layout changed; this cannot be verified from the supplied files. Updating golden hashes in the same PR as the implementation is routine, and I found no sign of masking a regression.

3. Main.swift line 66: it adds a call to checkGemmaTensorParallel. That function is not defined in the supplied units, so I cannot see whether it exists, what it asserts or whether it compiles. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a problem.

No security regression is identified in the supplied evidence. needs_deeper_review is true only because the tensor-parallel implementation and the new check function are outside the supplied units.
